Single-cell foundation models · breast cancer · survival

Cell states from two single-cell foundation models predict breast-cancer survival no better than a linear baseline

Zero-shot scGPT and Geneformer · marker-gene signatures · TCGA-BRCA and an independent METABRIC replication

Natalija Stepurko · October 2026 · natalija-stepurko.com

Do cell states found by single-cell foundation models carry prognostic information that a linear method misses? Cell states were defined in 50,002 cells from 152 donors of a breast-cancer atlas with zero-shot scGPT and Geneformer and with a linear baseline (principal components of highly variable genes, HVG-PCA), turned into marker-gene signatures and scored in 1,094 TCGA-BRCA tumours against outcome permutations, matched random gene sets and clinical references. In the pre-specified risk direction no representation's best signature cleared its family-wise permutation null (p = 0.20 HVG-PCA, 0.098 scGPT, 0.37 Geneformer), and both foundation models' margins over the baseline were negative (scGPT −0.021, Geneformer −0.039 in C-index). No pick showed a reproducible improvement over age and stage. With signatures fixed before outcomes were examined, all eight foundation-model-minus-baseline margins were negative in 1,979 METABRIC patients. The result concerns marker-gene projections of the tested checkpoints, not everything their embeddings encode.

All the code is public. Every number and figure on this page comes from the pipeline in this repository: atlas assembly, embeddings, the controls and the METABRIC replication.Natalija-Stepurko/single-cell-fm-probing

The question

Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT (Cui et al. 2024) and Geneformer (Theodoris et al. 2023) are pretrained on tens of millions of cells, and a common claim is that they learn cell biology that a linear analysis of the same data misses. For drug discovery and patient stratification the test that matters is whether that biology separates patients by outcome. This study asks whether cell states defined by these two models in a tumour atlas, carried into patient cohorts as marker-gene signatures, predict breast-cancer survival better than states from a linear baseline.

A fair benchmark

The three representations share everything except the representation itself: the same 50,002 cells, the same Leiden clustering, marker ranking and gene universe, the same scoring of each state's markers in 1,094 TCGA-BRCA tumours, and the same survival statistics. Each representation's pick is the state whose signature lies furthest above its random-gene floor. Every result is read against three controls:

  • Family-wise permutation null. Outcomes are permuted 10,000 times and the best of a representation's 201–369 signatures is kept each time, so the null includes picking a winner.
  • Random gene sets matched for size and expression. In breast cancer most random gene sets predict outcome (Venet et al. 2011); 200 per signature give its floor.
  • Clinical references. Age and stage, the PAM50 intrinsic subtype (Parker et al. 2009) and the published 11-gene proliferation score (Nielsen et al. 2010).

Headline result

No representation beats chance selection. In the pre-specified risk direction the best of each representation's signatures stays inside its family-wise null (p = 0.20 HVG-PCA, 0.098 scGPT, 0.37 Geneformer). Read in either direction (post hoc), HVG-PCA (p = 0.025) and scGPT (0.041) clear it; Geneformer (0.055) does not, a borderline result 2.0 Monte-Carlo standard errors above 0.05.

Neither foundation model is ahead of the baseline. Measured as distance above the random-gene floor, scGPT's pick trails the baseline's by 0.021 in C-index (95% interval −0.078 to +0.012) and Geneformer's by 0.039 (−0.084 to −0.001). Read in either direction the margins are −0.010 and −0.013, with intervals spanning zero.

Clinical information is far ahead. Age and stage alone reach a cross-validated C-index of 0.751. The picks reach 0.546–0.591 alone, selected on these patients; the published proliferation score, with no selection, reaches 0.569.

Added value over age and stage

Each pick was added to a Cox model of age and stage (1,072 patients, 142 deaths), with the signature re-selected inside every training fold so that the selection is paid for. No pick showed a reproducible improvement: the change in cross-validated C-index ranged from −0.0016 to +0.0008, and every pick's change spans zero across five repeats. The published proliferation score raised it by +0.008; once PAM50 subtype was in the model its change was −0.003.

Independent replication in METABRIC

The signatures, their directions and the replication criterion were fixed before METABRIC outcomes were examined. In 1,979 METABRIC patients (1,143 deaths) (Curtis et al. 2012; Pereira et al. 2016), every foundation-model-minus-baseline margin is negative; the 95% interval lies below zero for one of the four pre-specified comparisons and for all four post hoc ones. The published proliferation score replicates most strongly (overall-survival C-index 0.583 against a random-gene 95th percentile of 0.545).

What the states are

Four of the six picks are tumour-cell programmes whose bulk scores follow the intrinsic subtypes of breast cancer, in TCGA and again in METABRIC. The baseline's pre-specified pick is a single-dataset artefact, and Geneformer's protective pick a stress profile.

ε²: rank-based effect size of PAM50 subtype on the signature score (0: no association; the published proliferation score has 0.61). AUC: probability that a tumour of that subtype scores higher than one of another subtype.

Secondary result: donor mixing. The foundation-model embeddings produced fewer donor-specific states than HVG-PCA (9% of scGPT and 14% of Geneformer states draw at least 80% of their cells from one donor, against 41%). This did not translate into clearly stronger prognostic signatures: the best multi-donor state lies 0.074 (scGPT) and 0.035 (Geneformer) above its floor, against 0.075 for HVG-PCA; read in either direction the foundation models lead by 0.010 and 0.002, without an interval. The clusterings are stable under donor subsampling (mean adjusted Rand index 0.80–0.93).

What is new, and what was known

We found no prior study that defines cell states with foundation models in a tumour single-cell atlas, carries them into an independent bulk cohort as marker-gene signatures, compares them with a linear HVG-PCA arm passed through the identical pipeline, reads every result against matched random gene sets and a family-wise permutation null, and replicates the frozen signatures in a second cohort; to our knowledge the combination is new.

  • Single-cell states carried to bulk outcome. EcoTyper defined prognostic cell states across carcinomas (Luca et al. 2021). In breast cancer, Wu et al. 2021 related single-cell ecotypes to bulk outcome, and Chen A et al. 2026, whose collection supplies 63% of this atlas's cells, found that the states whose associations held across cohorts were protective. Scissor (Sun et al. 2022) uses the outcome to choose cells.
  • Foundation models and clinical outcome. Twelve single-cell foundation models offered limited advantages over simpler baselines for cancer patients' outcomes within single-cell cohorts (Roman et al. 2025); TCGA survival has been predicted from foundation-model embeddings of bulk profiles (Liu W et al. 2026).
  • Linear baselines. Simple baselines match foundation models in zero-shot cell-level tasks (Kedzierska et al. 2025) and perturbation prediction (Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025; Bendidi et al. 2024). Random gene sets predict breast-cancer outcome (Venet et al. 2011), the reason for the matched-random floor.

The result agrees with the limited foundation-model advantage reported by Roman et al. 2025, and the states that clear the null in the either-direction reading are protective, as were the cross-cohort survivors of Chen A et al. 2026.

Why it matters, and what it does not show

For drug discovery and patient stratification the result is a caution: here, states from zero-shot foundation-model embeddings did not give better prognostic signatures than a linear method applied to the same cells. The conclusion is limited to the checkpoints tested, scGPT whole-human and the 6-layer Geneformer V1, used zero-shot; neither saw malignant cells in pretraining, and cancer-adapted checkpoints such as CancerFoundation (Theus et al. 2024) were not tested. A marker-gene signature scored in bulk tumours is a lossy projection of a cell state, so the study tests whether the states transfer into bulk prognosis, not whether the embeddings contain prognostic information. It covers one indication, breast cancer, with 151 deaths in TCGA and short follow-up.

How the analysis was checked

The four predictions and their tests are written out in the design document. The code was audited against that design, and every place where the reported analysis departs from it is listed with its reason under deviations from the design. Unit tests, continuous integration and three reproduction tiers, from the distributed results up to a rebuild from scratch, cover the code.

Technical detail

The full study: methods and controls, the predictions, every number behind the summary, the secondary analyses, the deviations from the design, and how to reproduce it.

Methods and controls

The three representations share everything except the representation itself: the cells, the clustering method, the marker ranking, the gene universe, the scoring and the survival statistics.

Assemble the atlas

CELLxGENE Census release 2025-11-08: every breast-carcinoma disease label, primary data only, droplet-based 3′ and 5′ chemistries. After quality control, 50,002 cells from 152 donors in 8 datasets were sampled in proportion to their 48 annotated cell types. No batch correction was applied; 63% of the cells come from one collection (Chen A et al. 2026). 577 cells (1.2%) duplicate another atlas cell exactly (identical raw counts, same donor), between that collection's Global Atlas and its compartment datasets; they were not removed (49,425 unique cells).

Represent every cell three ways

HVG-PCA: the 2,000 most variable genes, log-normalised, reduced to 50 principal components fitted on this atlas. scGPT (Cui et al. 2024): the whole-human checkpoint, pretrained on non-malignant human cells, cell embedding from its classification token. Geneformer (Theodoris et al. 2023): the 6-layer V1 model, pretrained on a corpus that excluded malignant cells, mean-pooled cell embedding. Both models are used zero-shot and run in bfloat16 on CPU.

Find cell states

Leiden clustering (Traag et al. 2019) of each representation's 15-nearest-neighbour graph at resolutions 0.3, 0.5, 1.0; states with at least 200 cells are kept: 123 HVG-PCA, 67 scGPT and 71 Geneformer states.

Turn states into signatures

The top 25, 50, 100 marker genes of each state (Wilcoxon test against all other cells), drawn only from the 16,297 genes also measured in the bulk cohort (1,526 of them highly variable): 369, 201 and 213 signatures.

Score the signatures in TCGA-BRCA

Each of 1,094 primary tumours (Cancer Genome Atlas Network 2012) gets one score per signature: the mean of the signature genes' expression, each z-scored across patients. The ladder uses Harrell's C (Harrell et al. 1982) of that score alone, without covariates. A Cox model with age and stage gives each pick's hazard ratio, reported separately (Figure 2).

Pick and read

Each representation's pick is the signature furthest above its own random-gene floor across all nine settings (three resolutions × three marker counts), chosen on TCGA outcomes. The family-wise null tests the family maximum, the largest C among a representation's signatures; read against the same null, the picks have p = 0.67, 0.098, 0.59 (pre-specified; HVG-PCA, scGPT, Geneformer) and 0.072, 0.11, 0.16 (either direction). A patient bootstrap that re-selects the pick in every resample gives the P2 margins. P1–P4 are then read off the ladder.

The ladder of controls

Every C-index sits on a ladder of controls, and findings are stated as distances between rungs.

nullSurvival outcomes permuted across patients 10,000 times. In each permutation the largest C-index among all of a representation's 201–369 signatures is kept, so the null includes the selection of a winner. The family-wise p of the observed maximum is read against it, with its Monte-Carlo standard error; a p within two standard errors of 0.05 is marked borderline. The design specified 500 permutations; the results keep both sets, which agree on every verdict.
floor200 random gene sets per signature, matched for size and for mean-expression decile. In breast cancer most random gene sets are associated with outcome, largely through proliferation (Venet et al. 2011); the floor is what a gene list of that composition scores.
baselineThe HVG-PCA states, derived, scored and selected identically.
testThe scGPT and Geneformer states.
referencesAge + stage: cross-validated C 0.751 (1,072 patients; 0.732 on the 821 with a PAM50 call). PAM50 subtype alone (Parker et al. 2009): 0.525 cross-validated, 0.598 in sample. PAM50 + age + stage: 0.723. The published 11-gene proliferation score of PAM50 (Nielsen et al. 2010): C 0.569 against a floor mean of 0.480, permutation p = 0.0085 (10,000 permutations). Cross-validation is 5 × 5-fold.

What the baseline controls for

All three representations are computed from the same expression matrix, and their signatures are scored on the same bulk genes. Prognostic signal present in all three can come from that shared input: cell-type composition, tumour purity or proliferation. The baseline measures what the shared input yields through a linear, unsupervised representation, and every claim about the foundation models is stated as the margin over it.

The ladder in detail

Figure 1 in numbers, the either-direction reading, the progression-free interval and the ladder at each setting. Family-wise p-values are from 10,000 outcome permutations.

Pre-specified direction

The family maxima of all three representations stay inside their family-wise nulls in the pre-specified direction, and the margin-selected picks shown in Figure 1 do not clear the null in either reading (p = 0.67, 0.098 and 0.59 pre-specified; 0.072, 0.11 and 0.16 either direction). Geneformer's interval lies below zero, with its upper bound −0.001 near zero. scGPT's pick has the higher C-index (0.576 against 0.547) and also the higher floor (0.502 against 0.453); the baseline pick it is measured against is the single-dataset state described below and does not itself beat chance (p = 0.67).

Best margin: the largest C above the random-gene floor among the setting's signatures. Setting p: the family-wise p of the setting's largest C against the null restricted to that setting (500 permutations). At every setting both foundation models' best margin is below the baseline's, in both readings; in the risk direction no setting clears its own null (smallest p = 0.076, scGPT at resolution 1.0 with 50 markers).

Either direction (post hoc sensitivity analysis)

The pre-specified analysis reads the C-index in one direction: a signature scores high only when a higher score means worse survival. Protective signatures are common and include the largest departures from 0.5 (C down to 0.400). The sensitivity analysis reads every signature in the direction it acts on the full cohort; its floor is read the same way, and the family-wise null takes the largest max(C, 1 − C) over the same 10,000 permutations. P3 is tested for every representation, the baseline included, with 10,000 within-subtype permutations; pick and direction were fixed on the full cohort, which contains these patients.

The signatures that clear the null are the family maxima; for HVG-PCA and scGPT these are different states from the picks carried into added value, replication and Figure 4. Geneformer's family-wise p (0.055) lies 2.0 Monte-Carlo standard errors above 0.05: it does not clear, and the result is borderline. P2 still fails for both foundation models in this reading, and none of the pre-specified picks passes P3 (p = 0.38–0.40). Figure 4 shows the lead replicated signature as survival curves in TCGA, where it was selected: the HVG-PCA sensitivity pick, chosen by the rule in its caption.

Secondary endpoint: progression-free interval

The progression-free interval (PFI) has fewer events than OS in this cohort (145 against 151) and is analysed with the same statistics. The pattern is the same as for OS, with one difference: on PFI, Geneformer's either-direction family clears its null (p = 0.049, borderline), which it does not on OS.

Composition: donors and datasets with, in brackets, the share of the state's cells from the largest one, then the most frequent annotated cell type and its share. A state is flagged single-donor when one donor supplies at least 80% of its cells. ER, PR: oestrogen and progesterone receptor; HER2: the ERBB2 gene product.

Most picks are tumour-cell programmes that follow the intrinsic subtypes. In the risk direction, scGPT's pick is an ERBB2-containing luminal epithelial programme and Geneformer's a basal keratin programme. In the protective direction, HVG-PCA and scGPT both recover a luminal, oestrogen-responsive programme (GATA3, XBP1, AZGP1, TRPS1 in both lists). Their marker lists contain genes of the subtype axes that carry most prognostic information in breast cancer (Wirapati et al. 2008), and their bulk scores track PAM50 subtype (next section). Malignant cells cluster by patient in single-cell data (Tirosh et al. 2016): Geneformer's pre-specified pick (91% of its cells from one donor) and HVG-PCA's sensitivity pick (98%) are essentially one patient's tumour cells, and HVG-PCA's pre-specified pick (83%) is the single-dataset state below.

The baseline's pre-specified pick is a single-dataset artefact. Its cells are annotated as exhausted T cells, yet its markers are testis and colon genes (CEACAM7, TKTL1, FAM9C, INSL3), and none of the canonical T-cell markers (CD3D, CD3E, CD3G, CD2, CD4, CD8A, PTPRC) is among its 50 genes; it does include IKZF4, a regulatory-T-cell transcription factor, and the cell-cycle genes CDK2 and ERCC6L. It was picked because its random-gene floor is low (0.453), which makes its margin large although its C-index (0.547) is not. The pre-specified P2 margins are measured against it.

Geneformer's protective pick is a mixed-lineage state. Its markers are nuclear-retained transcripts and immediate-early genes, the profile of low-quality or dissociation-stressed cells.

Figure 5 places the picks in each representation's two-dimensional uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) of all 50,002 cells.

Do the states track PAM50 subtype? (post hoc)

Outcome-free: each pick's bulk score compared across intrinsic subtypes, in TCGA with the RNA-seq PAM50 call (842 patients) and in METABRIC with its PAM50 and claudin-low call (1,974 patients, no outcomes read).

Four of the six picks track subtype. scGPT's risk pick is highest in HER2-enriched tumours (one-vs-rest AUC 0.88) and Geneformer's in basal-like tumours (0.89); the luminal protective picks of HVG-PCA and scGPT are lowest in basal-like tumours (AUC 0.06 and 0.24). METABRIC tracks the same subtypes in the same direction (AUC 0.75, 0.90, 0.14 and 0.28). The baseline's single-dataset pick and Geneformer's stress state barely differ by subtype (ε² 0.03 and 0.04 in TCGA); the proliferation score, for comparison, has ε² 0.61. With PAM50 subtype, age and stage in the Cox model, the two foundation-model risk picks no longer point to risk (hazard ratio per standard deviation 0.90 and 0.91, nominal p 0.34 and 0.41), while the luminal protective picks keep hazard ratios below 1 (0.74 and 0.81); these hazard ratios are nominal, because every pick was selected on these outcomes.

Donor mixing (post hoc)

Every kept state at the three resolutions, each entering once through its 50-gene signature. States nest across resolutions, so the counts and the Fisher p are descriptive.

Malignant cells cluster by patient in single-cell data (Tirosh et al. 2016), and the atlas was pooled without batch correction. 50 of 123 HVG-PCA states (41%) draw at least 80% of their cells from one donor, against 6 of 67 scGPT (9%) and 10 of 71 Geneformer states (14%); the median state draws 40%, 18% and 15% of its cells from its largest donor. The foundation-model embeddings therefore produced fewer donor-specific states than HVG-PCA.

This did not translate into clearly stronger prognostic signatures. Among multi-donor states (no donor above 50%), the best margin above the floor in the risk direction is 0.075 for HVG-PCA, 0.074 for scGPT and 0.035 for Geneformer. Read in either direction it is 0.081, 0.091 and 0.083: the foundation models lead by 0.010 and 0.002, single values selected on TCGA outcomes and without an interval. In the either-direction reading the margin rises with the share from the largest donor in all three representations (Spearman ρ +0.29, +0.46 and +0.35): the states furthest from their floors tend to be dominated by one patient.

Are the states stable? (post hoc)

20 subsamples, each keeping 80% of the donors (122 of 152, the same draw for all representations); the neighbour graph and Leiden clustering are rebuilt on the kept cells with the settings of the main analysis.

The clusterings reproduce well: the mean adjusted Rand index between the subsample clustering and the full clustering restricted to the kept cells is 0.80–0.93 across representations and resolutions. The picks are less uniform. The best-matching subsample cluster shares on average 0.44 (scGPT's luminal ER pick) to 0.90 (the baseline's single-dataset pick) of a pick's cells (Jaccard index). The single-donor picks are reproduced almost exactly whenever their donor is kept, which is what one patient's cells clustering together predicts.

Clinical information

Each pick is added to a Cox proportional-hazards model of age and stage (1,072 patients, 142 deaths) and to age, stage and PAM50 subtype (821 patients, 116 deaths); Figure 2 shows the result. The ladder's C-indices are of the score alone; this section asks whether the score improves on what a clinician already has.

Age and stage alone reach a cross-validated C-index of 0.751 (1,072 patients); the PAM50 subtype call alone reaches 0.525 (821 patients). In this cohort PAM50 subtype does not raise the cross-validated C of age and stage either (0.732 against 0.733 on the 821 patients with a call), so the test has little room to show added value.

The hazard ratios in Figure 2 are nominal: every pick was chosen on the outcomes of these patients. The change in cross-validated C-index repeats the selection, and the choice of direction, inside every training fold, so it carries no selection. On that measure every pick's change in C spans zero across the five repeats. The luminal protective picks of HVG-PCA and scGPT keep nominal hazard ratios below 1 with PAM50 in the model (0.74 and 0.81 per standard deviation), but under nested selection they do not raise the cross-validated C-index. The published proliferation score (a fixed, published gene list, so free of selection) raises it by +0.008 over age and stage; once PAM50 is in the model its change is −0.003. Of the family maxima, only HVG-PCA's either-direction maximum raises it under nested selection (+0.007), and not once PAM50 is in the model.

All of a representation's states at once

A ridge-penalised Cox model with every state of a representation (50-gene signatures: 123 HVG-PCA, 67 scGPT, 71 Geneformer) plus age and stage does not improve on age and stage alone (Figure 8); differences of a few thousandths are within the spread across fold seeds. Gradient-boosted survival models (XGBoost, Cox objective, fixed hyperparameters) fall below age and stage alone with every representation's states (0.703–0.730), so they are not read as a comparison between representations.

Models within one section share their cross-validation folds; sections use different fold seeds, so the same model can differ by up to 0.009 between sections (age + stage 0.750–0.752; PAM50 + age + stage 0.723 and 0.732).

METABRIC in detail

The signatures, their directions and the replication criterion were fixed before METABRIC outcomes were examined.

METABRIC (Curtis et al. 2012; Pereira et al. 2016) is an expression-microarray cohort with long follow-up: 1,979 patients, 1,143 deaths (OS). Disease-specific survival (DSS) is the secondary endpoint; it censors deaths from other causes, leaving 646 events. Twelve signatures were frozen with their genes and TCGA directions: the six picks, the family maxima and the proliferation reference. A signature replicates on an endpoint if its C, read in the TCGA direction, exceeds the 95th percentile of its METABRIC floor and its age-adjusted hazard ratio, stratified by METABRIC cohort, points in the TCGA direction with p < 0.05.

C is read in the direction fixed in TCGA. Floor p95: 95th percentile of 200 matched random gene sets in METABRIC. HR/SD: age-adjusted hazard ratio per standard deviation of the score in that direction, stratified by METABRIC cohort. Borderline: C within two approximate Monte-Carlo standard errors of the floor p95 (normal approximation from the floor mean and p95). Within-subtype p: 1,000 outcome permutations; 0.001 is the smallest value attainable.

The replication shows no foundation-model advantage (Figure 3). The published proliferation score replicates most strongly (OS C = 0.583 against a floor 95th percentile of 0.545; DSS C = 0.637). Both HVG-PCA picks replicate. Of the foundation-model picks only Geneformer's risk pick meets the criterion, on DSS and by +0.0015, within Monte-Carlo error of the floor p95. Within luminal A tumours scGPT's protective pick has C = 0.562 with outcome-permutation p = 0.001; no random-gene floor was computed within subtypes, so this is a result, not a pre-specified replication. Geneformer's protective pick does not replicate.

Random gene sets predict survival in METABRIC. With 1,143 deaths, the matched-random floors have 95th percentiles of 0.52–0.57. Some signatures have hazard-ratio p-values below 10−5 and still do not beat random genes: Geneformer's risk pick (OS), scGPT's risk pick (OS and DSS). This is the effect described by Venet et al. 2011.

The baseline's artefact pick replicates on both endpoints. Why it replicates was not examined; its 50 genes include the cell-cycle genes CDK2 and ERCC6L.

How the analysis was checked: deviations from the design

The code was audited against the design document. Where the reported analysis differs from the design, or goes beyond it, the table gives the design, what is reported and why; post hoc analyses are labelled as such wherever they appear.

Deviations from the design, and analyses added after it (17 items)
itemdesignwhat is reported, and why
Clinical referenceThe PAM50 subtype call and a published prognostic signature.Age + stage, PAM50 subtype, and both together, each cross-validated on one set of patients; the published 11-gene proliferation score with its own random-gene floor and permutation p. A single in-sample model of PAM50 + age + stage on fewer patients would not be comparable with the single-score C-indices.
P1: what the family-wise null testsA family-wise permutation null for the best signature's C-index.The family maximum with its family-wise p, the statistic the null is built for; the margin-selected pick's p against the same null is reported beside it.
P1: number of permutations500 outcome permutations.10,000 permutations, for Monte-Carlo precision near 0.05; the 500-permutation values are kept and agree on every verdict.
P2: margin over the baselineTest against baseline, both read as distance above the floor; the bootstrap interval must exclude zero.Above-floor margin with 1,000 patient bootstraps that re-select each pick in every resample, so the interval includes the selection over hundreds of signatures; passes if the lower 2.5% bound is above zero.
P3: prognosis within subtypeAt least one foundation-model state is prognostic within a PAM50 subtype.Best within-subtype C against 10,000 within-subtype outcome permutations, for every representation, the baseline included, so that a pass can be compared with what the baseline reaches.
Monte-Carlo errorDecisions at α = 0.05.Every permutation p is given with its Monte-Carlo standard error, and a p within two standard errors of 0.05 is marked borderline.
P4: genes outside the HVG setFoundation-model signatures that pass P2 are enriched for non-HVG genes.Tested only if P2 passes, with a hypergeometric test against the scored-gene universe; P2 fails, so P4 is not applicable.
Ladder at each settingResolution and marker count are swept, and the ladder is reported at each setting.One pick per representation across all nine settings, paid for by a family-wise null over the same nine; the ladder at each setting, with its own null, is in the table under the ladder in detail.
Adjustment for age and stageCox models adjusted for age and stage in the primary model.The ladder C-index is of the score alone; adjustment enters through the added-value analysis: hazard ratios given age and stage, and the change in cross-validated C with the selection redone inside every fold.
Bootstrap intervals in the ladderPatient bootstrap intervals for the ladder.The whiskers in Figure 1 hold the pick fixed and are conditional on its selection; the selection-aware interval is the one used for P2.
Penalised reference modelsPAM50 subtype as a reference rung.The cross-validated C is the figure compared; the in-sample C of the penalised and unpenalised fits are given because they differ for PAM50 alone.
Secondary endpointProgression-free interval reported beside overall survival.PFI analysed with the same statistics.
Direction of effectC-index read in the risk direction only.Added post hoc: every signature also read in the direction it acts, labelled as a sensitivity analysis.
Clustering stabilityA separate diagnostic.Added post hoc: 20 donor subsamplings (80% of donors), adjusted Rand index per clustering and overlap per pick.
Subtype association and donor mixingNot in the design.Added post hoc and outcome-free: each pick's score by PAM50 subtype in TCGA and METABRIC, and the donor composition of every state against its margin.
Multivariable modelsNot in the design.Added: ridge and gradient-boosted Cox models of all of a representation's states with age and stage, the penalty applied to the state features only.
METABRIC replicationValidation of any shortlisted state in an independent cohort.All six picks, the family maxima and the proliferation reference, with signatures, directions and the replication criterion fixed before METABRIC outcomes were examined.

Reproduction

The pipeline is a Python package, scfm, whose stages are named commands. Each prints its plan with --dry-run before it touches data.

Stages, commands and reproduction tiers
stagedoes
dataassemble the single-cell atlas and the bulk cohort; harmonise genes
embedone embedding per cell for HVG-PCA, scGPT, Geneformer
statesLeiden clusters per representation → marker-gene signatures
stabilityclusters and picks under donor subsampling (needs the ladder; not part of 'all')
translatescore signatures in bulk; Cox; permutation null; matched-random floor; references
ladderassemble the ladder; patient bootstraps; test P1-P4
stratifycross-validated multivariable stratification: states vs age + stage
reportfigures
replicatefrozen signatures in METABRIC (run on its own; not part of 'all')
uv run scfm list                          # the stages, in order
uv run scfm run all --dry-run             # every stage's plan, nothing is run
uv run scfm run translate -- --endpoint PFI
make reproduce && make verify             # tier A, then compare checksums of the outputs

Three reproduction tiers

A, from the distributed results (about 40 min): rebuilds translate, ladder, stratify and report for OS and PFI from the distributed signatures. B, from the per-cell embeddings (not distributed): reruns states onward from the distributed cell list; the donor-subsampling stability stage adds about 25 min on 6 cores. C, from scratch (about 2 h 45 min on CPU, of which embedding is 1 h 44 min). Times are on a shared CPU machine. Tier A does not rebuild the atlas UMAP (Figure 5), which needs per-cell tables that are not distributed.

Tests and continuous integration

pytest covers the statistics, the stages' helpers and the Geneformer tokeniser, which is checked against the official tokeniser on a fixture; continuous integration runs the tests on every pull request. A small run executes every stage except replicate, both foundation models included, on 2,000 cells. Downloads are checksum-verified before use, and the atlas release and model versions are pinned.

Limits

  • Neither model saw malignant cells in pretraining. The scGPT whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on non-diseased cells and Geneformer's corpus excluded malignant cells, while most of the picks here are malignant-cell states. Cancer-adapted checkpoints, such as CancerFoundation (Theus et al. 2024) or the cancer-tuned Geneformer, were not tested.
  • Light checkpoints, zero-shot. scGPT whole-human and the 6-layer Geneformer V1 model, without fine-tuning, run on CPU. A negative result is a result about these checkpoints.
  • A bulk score is a lossy projection. The mean z-score of a state's markers mixes the state's abundance with tumour purity, proliferation and subtype; information in the embedding that its marker genes do not carry is not tested.
  • One atlas, no batch correction. 8 datasets, 3′ and 5′ chemistries, pooled without integration; one baseline pick is confined to a single dataset.
  • Single-donor states. Three of the six picks, and 50, 6 and 10 of the HVG-PCA, scGPT and Geneformer states, draw at least 80% of their cells from one donor.
  • Duplicate cells. 577 cells (1.2%) duplicate other cells across Chen et al.'s Global Atlas and its compartment datasets; they were not removed.
  • Power. 151 deaths among 1,094 TCGA patients, with short follow-up; the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource flags breast-cancer OS as needing longer follow-up (Liu J et al. 2018).
  • Selection in one cohort. The picks were chosen on TCGA outcomes. The family-wise null, the selection-aware bootstrap and the nested cross-validation pay for that choice within TCGA; METABRIC is the only out-of-sample test.
  • One indication. Breast cancer was chosen for cohort size and established references; nothing here extends to other tumours until it is run there.
